paragraph: Franklin Lakes runs on single-family houses, and the last six months brought 63 of them at a median of $1,860,000. The typical sale is a five-bedroom colonial with three full baths, which is what that price level buys here. Sale-to-list landed at exactly 1.00 with 41 percent of homes closing above asking and a median of 17 days on market, so call this competitive but not frenzied. Well-priced houses move quickly, and buyers should expect competition on the good ones without assuming every listing turns into a bidding war. Sales ranged from $580,000 to $4,850,000, so the median is the number to anchor on. Monthly medians bounced between $1,436,000 and $3,000,000, but with seven to twelve closings most months that is mix, not a price trend. What is readable is volume: it built steadily into June and July, with 19 closings in July, right on the normal seasonal arc. If the town follows the usual pattern, expect closings to taper modestly through fall before deep winter thins out. The townhouse and condo tier is too small to generalize from at four sales, and at a median of $2,012,500 it is not the lower-priced alternative some buyers expect.
